content_of_post_to_comment:
Some of my longest streaks 80-90 days have been mediated by blocks but blocks seem to come with a consequence of binging whenever a slight opportunity presents itself (e.g new laptop, unrestricted WiFi network, increase in privacy, loss of structure). If I want to override or circumvent a block, I can always do so with sufficient effort but the blocks essentially work when I somehow convince myself that accessing porn is impossible and stop trying. Sometimes something changes and I lose this conviction and then I binge all the porn that I may have missed out on during my streak. There is a crazy amount of curiosity that keeps me binging without end and unfortunately there is a limitless amount of porn available so there is no limit to how long I can go. I’ve felt tempted to not put the blocks back on because the binging is really bad. Unfortunately, once I discover a loophole I don’t seem to be able to stop myself without reimposing the blocks. I’ll relapse 5+ times in a day and get completely fatigued. Unfortunately this fatigue compromises healthy habits (e.g. eating, sleeping, going outside) and leaves me vulnerable to relapsing even more. There’s a window after extreme fatigue following a binge where I have space/time to take action and put new blocks because I’m so fatigued I am immune to relapsing for a few hours. But if I don’t take action within that period, I can get complacent thinking “im good now” but the unblocked site festers as curiosity in my mind and it’s incredibly difficult to not scratch that itch once I have scratched it once. The issue is that my blocks have had to get stricter and stricter as time has progressed. Once I blocked the initial main porn sites, I managed to discover new loopholes with foreign language sites or social media sites. Then I had to block those too. Then I discovered more loopholes through audio porn on Spotify and I had to block it too. Then I discovered AI could produce erotica and I had to block AI too. My brain seems to be too curious for its own good. It feels like an arms race between the addict in me and the man who wants to recover. Ultimately I know that long term recovery requires building mental fortitude to have the awareness to see temptations and watch them subside (essentially urge surfing). However, some waves are too big for me too surf and blocking helps me limit the metaphorical wave size to a manageable amount. But ocean keeps brewing more and more storms and I don’t know if I can train my surfing ability fast enough to keep up. Additionally if I fail to surf an urge, my urge surfing ability becomes compromised and I become more vulnerable.

Does anyone have any thoughts on how to manage this?
comment: The fact that you have a window after a binge where you're able to reinstall blocks seems like something you could build a plan around, rather than relying on feeling motivated in that moment. Maybe have the steps ready beforehand so you don't have to negotiate with yourself when you're exhausted. Also, a slip doesn't have to turn into a full-day binge; breaking that connection could matter as much as preventing the first relapse.
